scope: Prioritized omissions from this repository, verified against current primary documentation. This is a proposed benchmark backlog, not a ranking of unmeasured tools.
audit: The current guide covers 15 tool families. Large timings include SciPy RegularGridInterpolator/xarray.interp, xESMF, CDO, Pyresample nearest/Gaussian, rasterio/rioxarray/odc-geo, MIR, native HEALPix, ESMPy, Xugrid, UXarray and iris-esmf-regrid. A package's inclusion does not establish coverage of every backend or method.

prioritized_tools.name: xarray-regrid
prioritized_tools.methods: Linear, nearest, cubic, conservative and zonal statistics including most/least common classes
prioritized_tools.why: Adds a directly relevant lazy conservative implementation and categorical coarsening workflow. Its published chunk benchmark changes relative ordering with layout and skipna, making it particularly important for the new chunked tier.
prioritized_tools.overlap_existing: Separate package from the existing xarray.interp adapter. Linear interpolation overlaps xarray; conservative and mode-style aggregation extend the tested operations.
prioritized_tools.proposed_test: Use identical rectilinear grids, three chunk layouts, complete compute timers, missing fractions and normalization. Include categorical coarsening and an area-integral check.

prioritized_tools.name: CNES pyinterp
prioritized_tools.geometry: Rectilinear interpolation/conservative grids; separate scattered-point tree workflows
prioritized_tools.methods: Structured interpolation, conservative rectilinear remapping, scattered interpolation
prioritized_tools.why: Adds a distinct implementation exploiting separable rectilinear axes. Official documentation supports periodic longitude and distinguishes spherical/ellipsoidal areas and NaN normalization; these are central correctness cases in our survey.
prioritized_tools.overlap_existing: Overlaps SciPy/xarray point interpolation and xESMF conservative roles, but conservative cells follow meridians/parallels rather than ESMF great-circle edges. It is not a general curvilinear conservative substitute.
prioritized_tools.proposed_test: Compare structured target and scattered query APIs separately; include dateline padding/wrapping, explicit bounds, NaNs, normalized versus unnormalized coverage, and one-thread timings before optional parallel scaling.

prioritized_tools.name: MBTempest / MOAB
prioritized_tools.geometry: Spherical structured/unstructured meshes including cubed-sphere, regular lat/lon and icosahedral
prioritized_tools.methods: Overlap mesh construction and conservative weight generation; high-order and monotonic variants
prioritized_tools.why: The published E3SM/MOAB construction study includes this implementation, whereas our suite tests serial TempestRemap and NCO applying those maps. It is the most direct missing spherical construction candidate.
prioritized_tools.overlap_existing: Uses MOAB plus TempestRemap but has a distinct mesh/intersection workflow; it is not covered by an NCO application that reuses serial TempestRemap weights.
prioritized_tools.proposed_test: Use the same native closed spherical meshes for ESMF, TempestRemap and MBTempest; time conversion, overlap, weights and application separately and check common-domain conservation.

prioritized_tools.name: XRegrid
prioritized_tools.geometry: Structured grids and documented MPAS/ICON/UGRID/UXarray unstructured workflows
prioritized_tools.methods: ESMF-based regridding; documented unstructured nearest and conservative methods, reusable sparse weights and Dask support
prioritized_tools.why: Relevant alternative ESMF wrapper for distributed/chunked weight construction and application usability. Documentation includes performance claims, but local matched tests are needed before recommending it over xESMF.
prioritized_tools.overlap_existing: Shares the ESMF engine already exercised by xESMF/ESMPy/iris-esmf-regrid. Wrapper, sparse application and distribution can still change speed and usability; do not count it as an independent numerical kernel.
prioritized_tools.proposed_test: Compare identical ESMF methods/grids and equal thread/scheduler settings; check whether lazy execution is retained, sparse weights agree and masks/metadata survive. Record any triangulation and aggregation effects.
prioritized_tools.benchmark_caution: Performance guide includes an explicitly estimated xESMF timing at 0.1 degree; do not treat every table entry as a measured value. This backlog makes no numeric speed claim.

prioritized_tools.name: YAC
prioritized_tools.geometry: Supported spherical coupling grids with grid geometry and masks
prioritized_tools.methods: Conservative, nearest, average, spherical patch and configurable interpolation stacks
prioritized_tools.why: Adds a distinct coupling/remapping implementation and explicit fallback stacks, broadening beyond the currently tested ESMF/Tempest/CDO configurations.
prioritized_tools.overlap_existing: The repository does not explicitly exercise a YAC configuration; inclusion of CDO as a package is insufficient to claim YAC method coverage.
prioritized_tools.proposed_test: Start with first-order conservative and nearest on the same closed spherical fixtures; validate masks and covered-domain integral, then consider higher-order/fallback-stack behavior. Keep coupling communication costs distinct from map construction/application.

untested_operations_in_existing_tools.name: SciPy ndimage.map_coordinates
untested_operations_in_existing_tools.why: The existing SciPy adapter uses RegularGridInterpolator. This index-coordinate interpolation API supplies a different fast path for regularly spaced axes, including grid-wrap boundaries; it needs explicit coordinate-to-index conversion and separate boundary/NaN/dtype validation.

untested_operations_in_existing_tools.name: Pyresample gradient search, bilinear and scan-aware workflows
untested_operations_in_existing_tools.why: Current tests cover k-d-tree nearest/Gaussian, not the documented gradient-search or standalone bilinear algorithms. These have topology and interface constraints, so suitability and laziness cannot be inferred from the nearest adapter.

untested_operations_in_existing_tools.name: Native Iris area weighting
untested_operations_in_existing_tools.why: The package labelled iris in our timing suite uses iris-esmf-regrid ESMFAreaWeighted. Native iris.analysis.AreaWeighted is a different bounded-1D-axis scheme with different cell-edge geometry and is not measured by those results.

untested_operations_in_existing_tools.name: Higher-order remapping and repeated remap quality
untested_operations_in_existing_tools.why: Patch, second-order conservative and high-order/limited spherical variants are not established by the current single-remap nearest/bilinear/first-order results. Test convergence, bounds, discontinuities and long-cycle dissipation rather than ranking these only by smooth-field RMSE.
untested_operations_in_existing_tools.priority: Medium; expand accuracy protocol before performance ranking

not_distinct_kernel_priorities: GDAL command-line warp is useful for CLI/I/O usability coverage, but Rasterio and rioxarray already expose GDAL reprojection; it is not automatically a new interpolation engine.

GeoUtils and similar raster wrappers can provide useful workflow baselines, but first document their underlying resampling backend so wrapper overhead is not mistaken for a distinct numerical algorithm.
Chunked tests currently cover only xESMF, xarray and odc-geo. Missing chunked tests for an existing tool mean unknown execution behavior, not lack of Dask support.
